value.content: PALM BEACH COUNTY PLANNING, ZONING AND BUILDING DEPARTMENT ZONING DIVISION Application No.: ZV/PDD/DOA-2023-00955 Application Name: Johns PUD Control No./Name: 2021-00073 (Johns PUD) Applicant: Boca Raton Associates X, LLLP Owners: Boca Raton Associates XI, LLLP and Boca Raton Associates X, LLLP Agent: Boca Raton Associates X, LLLP - Gladys DiGirolamo and Ryan Vandenburg Telephone No.: (954) 753-1730, (954) 603-0324 Project Manager: Imene Haddad, AICP, Senior Site Planner Title: a Type 2 Variance Request: to allow an increase in wall height on 329.87 acres Title: an Official Zoning Map Amendment Request: to allow a rezoning from the Agricultural Residential (AR) Zoning District to the Planned Unit Development (PUD) Zoning District on 70.35 acres Title: a Development Order Amendment Request: to modify the Master Plan to add land area (70.35 acres) for a total 329.87 acres and to add units, and modify Conditions of Approval APPLICATION SUMMARY: The proposed request is for the 329.87-acre Johns PUD. The site was last approved by the Board of County Commissioners (BCC) for an Official Zoning Map Amendment to allow a rezoning from the Agricultural Residential (AR) Zoning District to the Planned Unit Development (PUD) Zoning District on January 27, 2022. The subject requests will modify the Master Plan in order to add land area (70.35 acres) and units (308 units) to the approved 259.52 acre PUD, and a variance to allow a 16-foot high wall on top of a 10-high berm within the perimeter landscape buffer along the east property line and a 16-foot high wall on top of a 5 high berm within the perimeter landscape buffer along the north property line. The Preliminary Master Plan (PMP) indicates a total of 987 units within eight Residential Pods (A through H). The new Pod H will be located on the west side of Lyon’s Road. In addition, the Plan indicates two recreation Pods, open space, and a 6.26-acre Civic Pod. Access is from Lyons Road and State Road 7. SITE DATA: Location: East and west side of Lyons Road, approx. 0.26 miles north of Glades Road Property Control Number(s) 00-42-43-27-05-077-0061;00-42-43-27-05-076-0040 00-42-43-27-05-077-0561;00-42-43-27-05-077-0562 00-42-43-27-05-077-0411 Future Land Use Designation: Low Residential, 3 units per acre (LR-3) Existing Zoning District: Planned Unit Development District (PUD) on 259.52 acres and Agricultural Residential District (AR) on 70.35 acres Proposed Zoning District: Planned Unit Development (PUD) Total Acreage: 329.87 acres Tier: Urban/Suburban Overlay District: N/A Neighborhood Plan: N/A CCRT Area: N/A Municipalities within 1 Mile N/A Future Annexation Area N/A Commissioner District Mayor Maria Sachs RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommends approval of the requests subject to the Conditions of Approval as indicated in Exhibits C-1 through C-3. ACTION BY THE ZONING COMMISSION (ZC): Scheduled January 11, 2024 ZC Hearing PUBLIC COMMENT SUMMARY: At the time of publication, Staff had received no contacts from the public regarding this application. PROJECT HISTORY: An official Zoning Map Amendment to allow a rezoning from the Agricultural Residential (AR) Zoning District to the Planned Unit Development PUD Zoning District was approved for the John West Development per PDD-2021-1174 on January 27, 2022. FINDINGS: When considering a Development Order application for a Type 2 Variance, the Zoning Commission shall consider Standards a through g listed under Article 2.B.7.E.6, Standards for Zoning Variance. The Standards and Staff Analyses are as indicated below. A Type 2 Variance that fails to meet any of these Standards shall be deemed adverse to the public interest and shall not be approved. a. Special conditions and circumstances exist that are peculiar to the parcel of land, building, or structure, that are not applicable to other parcels of land, structures, or buildings in the same district: APPLICANT’S RESPONSE: Johns PUD (formerly Johns West PUD) was previously approved for 679 ZLL and SF units through Resolution R-2022-0044. The subject site is adjacent to Olympic Heights High School which was approved in 1989 through Resolution R-1989-1166. Through the approval of the high school, numerous on-site athletic features were also approved. This included a football field with track, grandstands and pole lighting ranging in height from approx. 67 ft. to 100 ft. Additionally, the grandstands for the football fields are equipped with a speaker system and scoreboard, enhancing the field experience through live announcements. To the east of the football field along the south property line of the school site are 8 racquetball courts. These racquetball courts have approx. 21 ft. walls on the east, west and south side of the courts (see pictures below). To the north of these racquetball courts are 6 tennis courts as well as 4 basketball courts. And to the north of the football field are 2 baseball diamonds, complete with grandstands and a speaker system. The following aerial identifies all the athletic uses, while the yellow dots identify the location of the pole lighting that provides nighttime lighting for the facilities. There are a number of Special Conditions and Circumstances that exist that are peculiar to Johns PUD that are not applicable to other parcels of land, structures, or buildings in the same district. Zoning Commission January 11, 2024 Page 2 Application No. ZV/PDD/DOA -2023-00955 Johns PUD Proximity to School Facilities: The subject property is directly adjacent to the Olympic Heights High School that educates grades PK-12, with approximately 2,300 – 2,400 students attending. Unlike most residential developments, the subject site is in extremely close proximity to the outdoor facilities that generate substantial noise and visual impacts, such as the previously discussed stadium lighting, grandstands, and amplified sound systems. This proximity of these facilities to new residential development is not comparable to the majority of residential properties within Palm Beach County. Between Jupiter and Boca Raton, there are 17 Public High Schools (private schools were not identified as Olympic Heights is a public school). Only 3 of these High Schools are actually within Unincorporated Palm Beach County, where PBC staff would have reviewed and approved these schools. As part of Exhibit 1 below, 2 schools within a 5 mile radius of the subject site (Spanish River Community High School and Boca Raton High School) and the 3 schools within Unincorporated Palm Beach County have been located and a general distance has been provided identifying an estimate of the distance from the high school football fields to residential lot lines. The Applicant has reviewed all 17 schools identified, and with the exception of John Leonard High School and Royal Palm Beach Community High School (not within unincorporated PBC) and Santaluces High School (within Palm Beach County, part of Exhibit 1 below), all Public High School Football fields/stadiums are separated from the nearest residential development by either existing and established landscape buffers (Royal Palm Beach Community HS, William T. Dwyer High School), roadways (Palm Beach Gardens Community HS, Jupiter Community HS, Palm Beach Central HS, Lake Worth Community HS, Atlantic Community HS), canals (Wellington HS, Spanish River Community HS) or lakes (Park Vista Community HS, Boynton Beach Community HS, Palm Beach Lakes Community HS), and in many cases a combination of these features.
